plain_english: The security group 'web-servers-prod-sg' (sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890) allows inbound SSH (port 22) from any IP address on the internet (0.0.0.0/0). This means anyone in the world can attempt to log into your production web servers directly via SSH, with no network-level restriction.
why_it_matters: Attackers continuously scan the internet for open SSH ports. Once found, your servers become targets for brute-force credential attacks, exploitation of unpatched SSH vulnerabilities, and lateral movement into the rest of your infrastructure. A successful login grants full shell access to the server.

business_impact.data_risk: An attacker with SSH access can exfiltrate all data on the server and pivot to attached databases or S3 buckets.
business_impact.financial_risk: Ransomware deployment or cryptomining via a compromised server can result in unexpected AWS bills and business downtime.
business_impact.compliance_risk: Violates CIS AWS Foundations 4.1, PCI DSS 1.2.1, and NIST AC-17. A breach traced to this misconfiguration could trigger PCI DSS fines and mandatory forensic audits.

fix_steps.step: Remove the rule allowing SSH from all IPs on security group sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890.
fix_steps.cli_command: aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --region us-east-1 --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 --protocol tcp --port 22 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0

fix_steps.step: Add a new rule allowing SSH only from your trusted IP range (replace 203.0.113.0/24 with your VPN or office CIDR).
fix_steps.cli_command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --region us-east-1 --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 --protocol tcp --port 22 --cidr 203.0.113.0/24

fix_steps.step: Verify that the open rule is gone and only the trusted CIDR remains.
Consider switching to AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for SSH-less access, which requires no open inbound ports at all.

tldr: Your production web servers accept SSH login attempts from anywhere on the internet — restrict this to known IP addresses immediately to prevent unauthorized access.
